The schemabench_0206 database schema is used to store information about users, accounts, comments, posts, likes, friendships, messages, notifications, groups, and admins. The schema consists of 11 tables, each with its own set of columns and constraints.
The users table contains information about individual users, including their user ID, username, password, first name, middle name, last name, email, phone number, address, registration date, and description. The USER_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The USER_NAME column is unique and cannot be null. The PASSCODE column is not null and the FIRST_NAME, MIDDLE_NAME, and LAST_NAME columns are not null. The EMAIL column is not null and the PHONE_NUMBER and ADDRESS columns are optional. The REGESTRATION_DATE column is set to the current date and time by default. The IS_ADMIN column is a boolean that indicates whether the user is an admin or not. The DESCRIPTION_ column is a text field that can contain a description of the user.
The accounts table contains information about individual accounts, including their account ID, user ID, account type, and description. The ACCOUNT_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The USER_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The ACCOUNT_TYPE column is not null and the DESCRIPTION_ column is a text field that can contain a description of the account.
The comments table contains information about individual comments, including their comment ID, post ID, user ID, comment text, and comment date. The COMMENT_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The POST_ID column is a foreign key that references the POST_ID column in the posts table. The USER_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The COMMENT_TEXT column is a text field that can contain the comment text. The COMMENT_DATE column is set to the current date and time by default.
The posts table contains information about individual posts, including their post ID, user ID, content, post date, and post type. The POST_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The USER_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The CONTENT column is a text field that can contain the post content. The POST_DATE column is set to the current date and time by default. The POST_TYPE column is not null and can be used to categorize the post.
The likes table contains information about individual likes, including their like ID, post ID, user ID, and like date. The LIKE_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The POST_ID column is a foreign key that references the POST_ID column in the posts table. The USER_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The LIKE_DATE column is set to the current date and time by default.
The friendship table contains information about individual friendships, including their friendship ID, user ID 1, user ID 2, and friendship date. The FRIENDSHIP_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The USER_ID1 column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The USER_ID2 column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The FRIENDSHIP_DATE column is set to the current date and time by default.
The messages table contains information about individual messages, including their message ID, sender ID, receiver ID, text, message date, and is read. The MESSAGE_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The SENDER_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The RECEIVER_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The TEXT_ column is a text field that can contain the message text. The MESSAGE_DATE column is set to the current date and time by default. The IS_READ column is a boolean that indicates whether the message has been read or not.
The notifications table contains information about individual notifications, including their notification ID, user ID, notification text, notification date, and is read. The NOTIFICATION_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The USER_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The NOTIFICATION_TEXT column is a text field that can contain the notification text. The NOTIFICATION_DATE column is set to the current date and time by default. The IS_READ column is a boolean that indicates whether the notification has been read or not.
The groups table contains information about individual groups, including their group ID, group name, creator ID, and creation date. The GROUP_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The GROUP_NAME column is not null and can be used to identify the group. The CREATURE_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The CREATION_DATE column is set to the current date and time by default.
The admins table contains information about individual admins, including their admin ID, user ID, and group ID. The ADMIN_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The USER_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The GROUP_ID column is a foreign key that references the GROUP_ID column in the groups table.
The group_members table contains information about individual group members, including their group member ID, group ID, and user ID. The GROUP_MEMBER_ID column is the primary key and is set to auto-increment. The GROUP_ID column is a foreign key that references the GROUP_ID column in the groups table. The USER_ID column is a foreign key that references the USER_ID column in the users table. The JOIN_DATE column is set to the current date and time by default.
Overall, the schemabench_0206 database schema is designed to store information about users, accounts, comments, posts, likes, friendships, messages, notifications, groups, and admins. Each table has its own set of columns and constraints, and the relationships between the tables are established through foreign keys. The schema is designed to be flexible and scalable, allowing for the addition of new tables and columns as needed.

1) Background / Context:

The project involves the development of a social media platform. This platform is designed to facilitate user interaction and content sharing, leveraging various social media functionalities such as posting, commenting, liking, and messaging. The system architecture is based on a relational database schema, which interlinks multiple data tables to capture user activities and social connections.

2) Objectives:

- To create a robust social media database (`SocialMediaDatabase`) that supports essential social networking functionalities.
- To ensure scalable and secure user interactions, including content creation, communication, and social engagement.
- To facilitate efficient data management and retrieval through relational links among tables.

3) Stakeholders & Users:

- End Users: Individuals who will register and actively participate on the platform by sharing content, interacting with other users, and managing personal accounts.
- Administrators: Users with elevated permissions to oversee platform activities, manage user-generated content, and moderate group interactions.
- Developers: Technical personnel responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining the database and platform functionalities.

4) Functional Descriptions:

- User Management: Users can register, log in, and manage personal profiles. Registration information is stored in the `users` table.
- Account Management: Users can have different types of accounts, managed via the `accounts` table and linked to the main `users` table.
- Content Creation & Interaction:
  - Users can create posts (`posts` table) and others can comment on them (`comments` table).
  - Users can like posts (`likes` table) to express appreciation.
- Social Connections: 
  - Users can form friendships (`friendship` table).
  - Direct communication is facilitated through private messaging (`messages` table).
- Group Interactions:
  - Users can create and join groups (`groups_` and `group_members` tables).
  - Groups can have administrators assigned to manage group activities (`admins` table).
- Notifications: Users receive notifications (`notifications` table) about various activities involving their account.
  
5) Non-Functional Descriptions:

- Scalability: The system should support a growing number of users and content without performance degradation.
- Security: User data, particularly passwords, must be securely stored and managed.
- Reliability: The platform should ensure data integrity and availability, preventing loss or corruption of user data.
- Usability: The system interfaces should be intuitive, promoting ease of use for users with varying technical expertise.

-- Schema for database: schemabench_0206
CREATE TABLE `users` (
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  `passcode` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `first_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `middle_name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `last_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `email` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `phone_number` varchar(20) DEFAULT NULL,
  `address` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `registration_date` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `is_admin` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  `description_` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `accounts` (
  `account_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `account_type` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `description_` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`account_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `accounts_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `comments` (
  `comment_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `post_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `comment_text` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `comment_date` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`comment_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `comments_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`post_id`) REFERENCES `posts` (`post_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `comments_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `posts` (
  `post_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `content` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `post_date` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `post_type` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`post_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `posts_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `likes` (
  `like_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `post_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `like_date` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`like_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `likes_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`post_id`) REFERENCES `posts` (`post_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `likes_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `friendships` (
  `friendship_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id1` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id2` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `friendship_date` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`friendship_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `friendships_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id1`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `friendships_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id2`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `messages` (
  `message_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `sender_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `receiver_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `text_` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `message_date` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `is_read` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (`message_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `messages_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`sender_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `messages_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`receiver_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `notifications` (
  `notification_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `notification_text` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `notification_date` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  `is_read` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (`notification_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `notifications_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `groups` (
  `group_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `group_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `creator_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `creation_date` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`group_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `groups_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`creator_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `admins` (
  `admin_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `group_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`admin_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `admins_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `admins_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`group_id`) REFERENCES `groups` (`group_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `group_members` (
  `group_member_id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `group_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `join_date` datetime NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
  PRIMARY KEY (`group_member_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `group_members_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`group_id`) REFERENCES `groups` (`group_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `group_members_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
